problem: The installed system passed 70/90 suite goals with the screen awake, against 88/90 three weeks earlier. The existing dispatch fix for 'Context metadata exceeds planner budget' did not change the result: 70/90 in all three runs.
change: The failing goal was reproduced on a copy of the live database. The records added after the memory loop push a context that fitted back over the 2,500-character budget, by 32 characters. ARIES_PLAN_CONTEXT_FIT drops the lowest-ranked memories until the context fits. ARIES_PLANNER_PER_CAP_GRAMMAR (from R1b) removes the other cause, arguments attached to a clarification decision. With the owner's approval the live aries-core was moved to the current source through a systemd drop-in on a fixed worktree (~/aries-deploy). The source was first measured without the flags, then with them.
validation: Current source without the remedies: 70/71/70 of 90. With them: 79/79/79 of 90. Context-budget failures fell from 9 to 0 and invalid planner outputs from 7 to 1. tests/test_p1_remedies.py: 7 of 400 random contexts fail with the dispatch fix alone, 0 with the fit.
limitations: False success did not fall (8-10 of 90). Five multi-step goals now end on an ungrounded clarification. The long goals take longer, because they now run instead of failing at once (p90 17-33 s). Two lessons. A remedy that targets the symptom's name ('metadata') can miss the real overflow, so reproduce on real data before calling a fix done. A figure drawn while a run is still writing its results must skip unfinished runs.
